verses: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ شَىْءٌ عَظِيمٌ
يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَهَا تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمَّآ أَرْضَعَتْ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُكَٰرَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُكَٰرَىٰ وَلَٰكِنَّ عَذَابَ ٱللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ
وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطَٰنٍ مَّرِيدٍ
كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ مَن تَوَلَّاهُ فَأَنَّهُۥ يُضِلُّهُۥ وَيَهْدِيهِ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ فَإِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍ مُّخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوٓا۟ أَشُدَّكُمْ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُتَوَفَّىٰ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْـًٔا وَتَرَى ٱلْأَرْضَ هَامِدَةً فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ وَأَنۢبَتَتْ مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۭ بَهِيجٍ
ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنَّهُۥ يُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَأَنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
وَأَنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهَا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ
وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَلَا هُدًى وَلَا كِتَٰبٍ مُّنِيرٍ
ثَانِىَ عِطْفِهِۦ لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُۥ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا خِزْىٌ وَنُذِيقُهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ عَذَابَ ٱلْحَرِيقِ
ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّٰمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ

وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعْبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍ فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُۥ خَيْرٌ ٱطْمَأَنَّ بِهِۦ وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةَ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْخُسْرَانُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
يَدْعُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُۥ وَمَا لَا يَنفَعُهُۥ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلضَّلَٰلُ ٱلْبَعِيدُ
يَدْعُوا۟ لَمَن ضَرُّهُۥٓ أَقْرَبُ مِن نَّفْعِهِۦ لَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَوْلَىٰ وَلَبِئْسَ ٱلْعَشِيرُ
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ جَنَّٰتٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ
مَن كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَن لَّن يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ فَلْيَنظُرْ هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُۥ مَا يَغِيظُ
وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهْدِى مَن يُرِيدُ

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلْمَجُوسَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ

أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ وَكَثِيرٌ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ
هَٰذَانِ خَصْمَانِ ٱخْتَصَمُوا۟ فِى رَبِّهِمْ فَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيَابٌ مِّن نَّارٍ يُصَبُّ مِن فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ ٱلْحَمِيمُ
يُصْهَرُ بِهِۦ مَا فِى بُطُونِهِمْ وَٱلْجُلُودُ
وَلَهُم مَّقَٰمِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ
كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓا۟ أَن يَخْرُجُوا۟ مِنْهَا مِنْ غَمٍّ أُعِيدُوا۟ فِيهَا وَذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابَ ٱلْحَرِيقِ
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ جَنَّٰتٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ وَلُؤْلُؤًا وَلِبَاسُهُمْ فِيهَا حَرِيرٌ
وَهُدُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلطَّيِّبِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ وَهُدُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلْنَٰهُ لِلنَّاسِ سَوَآءً ٱلْعَٰكِفُ فِيهِ وَٱلْبَادِ وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍۭ بِظُلْمٍ نُّذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لِإِبْرَٰهِيمَ مَكَانَ ٱلْبَيْتِ أَن لَّا تُشْرِكْ بِى شَيْـًٔا وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْقَآئِمِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ
وَأَذِّن فِى ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ
لِّيَشْهَدُوا۟ مَنَٰفِعَ لَهُمْ وَيَذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ فِىٓ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْلُومَٰتٍ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْبَآئِسَ ٱلْفَقِيرَ
ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا۟ تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا۟ نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا۟ بِٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ

ذَٰلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ حُرُمَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّهُۥ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمُ إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ فَٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ ٱلرِّجْسَ مِنَ ٱلْأَوْثَٰنِ وَٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ قَوْلَ ٱلزُّورِ
حُنَفَآءَ لِلَّهِ غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ بِهِۦ وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتَخْطَفُهُ ٱلطَّيْرُ أَوْ تَهْوِى بِهِ ٱلرِّيحُ فِى مَكَانٍ سَحِيقٍ
ذَٰلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ شَعَٰٓئِرَ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقْوَى ٱلْقُلُوبِ
لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَٰفِعُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ثُمَّ مَحِلُّهَآ إِلَى ٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ
وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنَا مَنسَكًا لِّيَذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ فَإِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ فَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلِمُوا۟ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلْمُخْبِتِينَ
ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ وَٱلْمُقِيمِى ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ

وَٱلْبُدْنَ جَعَلْنَٰهَا لَكُم مِّن شَعَٰٓئِرِ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمْ فِيهَا خَيْرٌ فَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا صَوَآفَّ فَإِذَا وَجَبَتْ جُنُوبُهَا فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرْنَٰهَا لَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمْ لِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ خَوَّانٍ كَفُورٍ
أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا۟ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ

ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَوَٰتٌ وَمَسَٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًا وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
ٱلَّذِينَ إِن مَّكَّنَّٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَوُا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَمَرُوا۟ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا۟ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ وَلِلَّهِ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْأُمُورِ
وَإِن يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَعَادٌ وَثَمُودُ
وَقَوْمُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ
وَأَصْحَٰبُ مَدْيَنَ وَكُذِّبَ مُوسَىٰ فَأَمْلَيْتُ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهُمْ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ
فَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَا وَهِىَ ظَالِمَةٌ فَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَبِئْرٍ مُّعَطَّلَةٍ وَقَصْرٍ مَّشِيدٍ
أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ يَعْقِلُونَ بِهَآ أَوْ ءَاذَانٌ يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَى ٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ وَلَٰكِن تَعْمَى ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِى فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ
وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِٱلْعَذَابِ وَلَن يُخْلِفَ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُۥ وَإِنَّ يَوْمًا عِندَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ
وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَمْلَيْتُ لَهَا وَهِىَ ظَالِمَةٌ ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهَا وَإِلَىَّ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
قُلْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ
وَٱلَّذِينَ سَعَوْا۟ فِىٓ ءَايَٰتِنَا مُعَٰجِزِينَ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْجَحِيمِ

وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ وَلَا نَبِىٍّ إِلَّآ إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰٓ أَلْقَى ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ فِىٓ أُمْنِيَّتِهِۦ فَيَنسَخُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يُلْقِى ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ ثُمَّ يُحْكِمُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
لِّيَجْعَلَ مَا يُلْقِى ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ فِتْنَةً لِّلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ وَٱلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ لَفِى شِقَاقٍۭ بَعِيدٍ
وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمَ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَتُخْبِتَ لَهُۥ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
وَلَا يَزَالُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فِى مِرْيَةٍ مِّنْهُ حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ
ٱلْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلَّهِ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فِى جَنَّٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ
وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ قُتِلُوٓا۟ أَوْ مَاتُوا۟ لَيَرْزُقَنَّهُمُ ٱللَّهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًا وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
لَيُدْخِلَنَّهُم مُّدْخَلًا يَرْضَوْنَهُۥ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ
ذَٰلِكَ وَمَنْ عَاقَبَ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبَ بِهِۦ ثُمَّ بُغِىَ عَلَيْهِ لَيَنصُرَنَّهُ ٱللَّهُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ
ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُولِجُ ٱلَّيْلَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِى ٱلَّيْلِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌۢ بَصِيرٌ
ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ هُوَ ٱلْبَٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْكَبِيرُ
أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَتُصْبِحُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ
لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ

أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱلْفُلْكَ تَجْرِى فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِۦ وَيُمْسِكُ ٱلسَّمَآءَ أَن تَقَعَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ
وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْيَاكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَكَفُورٌ
لِّكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنَا مَنسَكًا هُمْ نَاسِكُوهُ فَلَا يُنَٰزِعُنَّكَ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ وَٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ إِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
وَإِن جَٰدَلُوكَ فَقُلِ ٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
ٱللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ فِى كِتَٰبٍ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ
وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِۦ سُلْطَٰنًا وَمَا لَيْسَ لَهُم بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ وَمَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ مِن نَّصِيرٍ

وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتٍ تَعْرِفُ فِى وُجُوهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلْمُنكَرَ يَكَادُونَ يَسْطُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِنَا قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَعَدَهَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ فَٱسْتَمِعُوا۟ لَهُۥٓ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَن يَخْلُقُوا۟ ذُبَابًا وَلَوِ ٱجْتَمَعُوا۟ لَهُۥ وَإِن يَسْلُبْهُمُ ٱلذُّبَابُ شَيْـًٔا لَّا يَسْتَنقِذُوهُ مِنْهُ ضَعُفَ ٱلطَّالِبُ وَٱلْمَطْلُوبُ
مَا قَدَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
ٱللَّهُ يَصْطَفِى مِنَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ رُسُلًا وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌۢ بَصِيرٌ
يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ ٱلْأُمُورُ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱرْكَعُوا۟ وَٱسْجُدُوا۟ وَٱعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ وَٱفْعَلُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ

وَجَٰهِدُوا۟ فِى ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦ هُوَ ٱجْتَبَىٰكُمْ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ مِن قَبْلُ وَفِى هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيْكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ فَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعْتَصِمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوْلَىٰكُمْ فَنِعْمَ ٱلْمَوْلَىٰ وَنِعْمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ

Only in Telipinu myth, first version: the god's anger and departure (CTH 324.1 §1-4): A god becomes angry and departs; mist seizes the windows, smoke the house, the hearth logs and the gods on the altar are stifled; Smoke envelops house or people as a calamity [divergence between the texts]; In the god's absence the ewe rejects her lamb and the cow her calf.

Only in The quake of the Hour and the proofs from embryo and rain: Some are returned to the most abject age so that after knowing they know nothing; The quake of the Hour: every nursing mother forgets her suckling, every pregnant one miscarries, people seem drunk though not drunk; Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped; In the catastrophe the father disowns his wife and the mother her child ('This is not my child'); In the catastrophe mothers, cows or she-camels no longer care for their young; God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews; On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls; Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

leads.title: The chosen place; profane slaughter; blood prohibition ↔ Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Who chose or founded the single sanctuary of sacrifice, and when [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 15.5.

Only in The chosen place; profane slaughter; blood prohibition: Do not inquire how the nations served their gods in order to imitate them; Every man doing what is right in his own eyes; Meat may be slaughtered and eaten anywhere, like gazelle and deer, when far from the sanctuary; Rejoice before God with sons, daughters, slaves and the Levite; Blood is the life; do not eat it but pour it on the ground like water; After crossing the sea the people see idol-worshipers and ask the prophet for a god like theirs; God causes his name to dwell at the chosen place; Sacrifice only at the place God will choose to make his name dwell; Command to smash altars, standing stones and Asherah poles and burn idols; Nations burn their sons and daughters in fire to their gods; Pagan worship on high mountains, hills and under every green tree.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); Whether the deity eats (receives) the food and drink of the offerings [divergence between the texts]; The deity shows or assigns to the builder the site (old foundation) of the deity's house; and 14 more.

matches.label: Who chose or founded the single sanctuary of sacrifice, and when
matches.note: Deut 12: ha-māqôm ʾăšer yivḥar YHWH, a place God will choose in the future, unnamed and linked to no patriarch; Q 22:26: bawwaʾnā li-Ibrāhīma makāna l-bayti, the place of the House was assigned to Abraham in the past and is 'the Ancient House' (al-bayt al-ʿatīq). passages.text: כִּ֠י אִֽם אֶל הַמָּק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ מִכָּל שִׁבְטֵיכֶ֔ם לָשׂ֥וּם אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם לְשִׁכְנ֥וֹ תִדְרְשׁ֖וּ וּבָ֥אתָ שָֽׁמָּה

כִּ֡י אִם לִפְנֵי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ תֹּאכְלֶ֗נּוּ בַּמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִבְחַ֜ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶיךָ֮ בּוֹ֒ אַתָּ֨ה וּבִנְךָ֤ וּבִתֶּ֨ךָ֙ וְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וַאֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְהַלֵּוִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֑יךָ וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֗ לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל מִשְׁלַ֥ח יָדֶֽךָ
وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لِإِبْرَٰهِيمَ مَكَانَ ٱلْبَيْتِ أَن لَّا تُشْرِكْ بِى شَيْـًٔا وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْقَآئِمِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ
ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا۟ تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا۟ نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا۟ بِٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ

matches.label: What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God
matches.note: Deut prescribes the blood: poured on the ground like water (ʿal hā-ʾāreṣ tišpəkennû ka-mmāyim) or on the altar of YHWH (wə-dam zəvāḥêkā yiššāpēk ʿal mizbaḥ YHWH); Q 22:37 says neither its flesh nor its blood reaches God (lan yanāla llāha ... dimāʾuhā), so no blood rite.

لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمْ لِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

passages.text: וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֞ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אַתָּ֨ה וּבִנְךָ֣ וּבִתֶּךָ֮ וְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וַאֲמָתֶךָ֒ וְהַלֵּוִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ וְהַגֵּ֛ר וְהַיָּת֥וֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבֶּ֑ךָ בַּמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִבְחַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן שְׁמ֖וֹ שָֽׁם
וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֖ בְּחַגֶּ֑ךָ אַתָּ֨ה וּבִנְךָ֤ וּבִתֶּ֨ךָ֙ וְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וַאֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְהַלֵּוִ֗י וְהַגֵּ֛ר וְהַיָּת֥וֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ
لِّيَشْهَدُوا۟ مَنَٰفِعَ لَهُمْ وَيَذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ فِىٓ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْلُومَٰتٍ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُم مِّنۢ بَهِيمَةِ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْبَآئِسَ ٱلْفَقِيرَ

leads.title: Levitical dues; forbidden divination; the prophet like Moses ↔ Rejected prophets, ruined towns, the thousand-year day and Satan's insertion

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Levitical dues; forbidden divination; the prophet like Moses: Be wholehearted (tamim) with God; A prophecy that does not come true shows the prophet spoke presumptuously; Priest's due: shoulder, two cheeks and stomach of the sacrifice, and first of the fleece; Duty to accept a prophet God will send later [divergence between the texts]; How God's word reaches the prophet [divergence between the texts]; A future prophet promised in the earlier scripture [response between the texts]; A future prophet 'from among them' [divergence between the texts]; Whether the dead may be consulted, or would persuade the living if they spoke [contrast between the texts]; False prophet put to death [divergence between the texts]; God sent before only men, inspired, from the people of the towns; Messengers are sent to people from among themselves; People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate; and 9 more.

Only in Rejected prophets, ruined towns, the thousand-year day and Satan's insertion: Destroyed towns lie fallen on their roofs, with an abandoned well and a lofty palace; It is not the eyes that are blind but the hearts within the breasts; Satan casts something into every prophet's recitation or wish; God abrogates it and confirms his verses; Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them [divergence between the texts]; YHWH will be king over all the earth; in that day YHWH will be one and his name one; A thousand years in God's sight are like yesterday when it passes, or a watch in the night; Scoffers ask the prophet to hasten the punishment; it is held back only by an appointed term and will come suddenly; The listeners walk among the dwellings of generations God destroyed, a sign; A foolish people who have eyes but do not see and ears but do not hear; The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

leads.finding: Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them

units.title: Levitical dues; forbidden divination; the prophet like Moses
Rejected prophets, ruined towns, the thousand-year day and Satan's insertion

matches.label: Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them
matches.note: Deut 18:20-22: a prophet who presumes (yāzîd) to speak a word God did not command shall die (û-mēt ha-nnāvîʾ ha-hûʾ); the word is known false when it does not come to pass (bə-zādôn dibbərô). Q 22:52: before you no messenger or prophet was sent but when he wished Satan cast into his wish (alqā sh-shayṭānu fī umniyyatihi), and God abrogates (yansakhu) what Satan casts. A false insertion is the prophet's capital guilt in Deut, a universal hazard that God himself cancels in the Quran.

passages.text: אַ֣ךְ הַנָּבִ֡יא אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָזִיד֩ לְדַבֵּ֨ר דָּבָ֜ר בִּשְׁמִ֗י אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא צִוִּיתִיו֙ לְדַבֵּ֔ר וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔ר בְּשֵׁ֖ם אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וּמֵ֖ת הַנָּבִ֥יא הַהֽוּא

leads.title: Jerusalem the exposed foundling, God's bride and the faithless harlot ↔ Six communities judged; all things prostrate; garments of fire and bracelets of gold
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Catalogue of bridal finery: embroidered cloth, tahash sandals, linen, silk, bracelets, necklace, nose-ring, earrings and a crown (weight 7.3); In paradise the righteous are adorned with gold bracelets and pearls and wear silk (weight 7.3). Pair score 14.7.

Only in Jerusalem the exposed foundling, God's bride and the faithless harlot: The adorned bride trusts in her beauty and plays the harlot with every passer-by; Sons and daughters born to God are slaughtered and offered to idols as food; A newborn girl is cast into the open field unwashed, unsalted and unswaddled, with her navel cord uncut, loathed on the day of her birth; God spreads his garment-wing over the grown foundling, swears a covenant and takes the city as his wife, bathing, anointing, clothing and adorning her; Unlike other harlots, the city pays fees to her lovers instead of receiving them; God passes by the infant wallowing in her blood and says twice 'In your blood, live!'; The unfaithful wife makes male images (tsalmei zakhar) from the gold and silver God gave her and fornicates with them; Political alliances with Egypt, Assyria and Chaldea pictured as harlotry with lovers ('big of flesh'); An assembly stones the adulteress and hacks her with swords and burns her houses before many women; God gathers the adulteress's lovers, strips her naked before them and hands her over to be judged; Jerusalem's origin is Canaanite: 'your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite'; Man asked to spread his garment-wing over a woman as a sign of marriage; and 3 more.

Only in Six communities judged; all things prostrate; garments of fire and bracelets of gold: Hooked maces of iron (maqāmiʿ) drive back those who try to escape hell; God will judge between believers, Jews, Sabians, Christians, Magians and polytheists on resurrection day; In hell the unbelievers are cut garments of fire and boiling water is poured on their heads, melting their insides and skins; The place of humans in the worship offered by all creation [divergence between the texts]; All in heaven and earth prostrate to God: sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, beasts and many humans; The host of heaven bows down to God; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

leads.title: Gog of Magog invades the land dwelling at the navel of the earth ↔ The quake of the Hour and the proofs from embryo and rain
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls (weight 6.4). Pair score 6.4.

Only in Gog of Magog invades the land dwelling at the navel of the earth: The invader plots to attack a quiet people dwelling securely in unwalled villages without bars or gates, to seize plunder; Gog's coalition: Persia, Cush, Put, Gomer with all its hordes, Beth-togarmah from the far north, many peoples; God asks 'Are you the one of whom I spoke in former days through my servants the prophets?'; God turns the invader around and puts hooks in his jaws to drag him out with all his army; The invading host comes up like a storm, like a cloud covering the land; Every man's sword is turned against his brother in the enemy host; Gog is summoned 'after many days', 'in the latter years / end of days', against a land restored from the sword; Restored Israel dwells 'on the navel of the earth' (tabbur ha-arets); God judges Gog with pestilence, blood, torrential rain, hailstones, fire and sulfur; Sheba, Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish ask the invader 'Have you come to take plunder?'; Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince (nesi rosh) of Meshech and Tubal, an eschatological invader [divergence between the texts]; The final invader comes from the farthest recesses of the north (yarketei tsafon); and 10 more.

Only in The quake of the Hour and the proofs from embryo and rain: Some are returned to the most abject age so that after knowing they know nothing; In catastrophe mothers abandon their young and pregnancy fails [divergence between the texts]; The quake of the Hour: every nursing mother forgets her suckling, every pregnant one miscarries, people seem drunk though not drunk; Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped; In the catastrophe the father disowns his wife and the mother her child ('This is not my child'); In the catastrophe mothers, cows or she-camels no longer care for their young; God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews; Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

leads.title: Abraham's treaty with Abimelech at Beersheba ↔ Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Abraham's treaty with Abimelech at Beersheba: Patriarch plants a tamarisk and calls on El Olam, the Everlasting God; Seven ewe lambs given as witness to a well-ownership oath (Beersheba); Dispute over a well resolved by an oath-treaty with a local king; In a named generation people begin to call on the name of the LORD.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; Whether the deity eats (receives) the food and drink of the offerings [divergence between the texts]; The deity shows or assigns to the builder the site (old foundation) of the deity's house; and 15 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Worshipping what can neither harm nor benefit you (weight 6.8); Idols of wood and stone that cannot see, hear, eat or smell (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.9.

Only in The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes: Woe to one who makes his neighbor drunk in order to gaze on his nakedness; The prophet stations himself on his watchpost to see what God will answer to his complaint; 'The righteous shall live by his faith (emunah)'; A series of 'woe' (hoy) taunt-sayings against an oppressor; The stone cries out from the wall and the beam answers from the woodwork; The vision is for an appointed time; though it tarry, wait for it, for it will surely come; Write the vision plainly on tablets so that a runner may read it; Woe to the one who says to wood 'Awake!' and to dumb stone 'Arise!'; there is no breath in it; The earth will be full of the knowledge of YHWH as the waters cover the sea; The arrogant man's appetite is wide as Sheol and like Death never satisfied, gathering all nations; Peoples labor only for fire and nations weary themselves for nothing; 'Hush (has) before YHWH, all the earth', for he is in his holy temple or has roused himself; and 6 more.

Only in Those who dispute about God and those who worship on an edge: Taunt: whoever thinks God will not help him, let him stretch a rope to the sky, then cut it, and see if his rage is removed; Some worship God 'on an edge': content in good fortune, turning away when tested; How a worshipper responds to good fortune and to misfortune sent by God [contrast between the texts]; Piety that holds only while fortune lasts, put to the test by misfortune; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The quake of the Hour: every nursing mother forgets her suckling, every pregnant one miscarries, people seem drunk though not drunk (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Oracle against Babylon; the Day of YHWH darkens the heavens: Babylon, glory of kingdoms, will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah; Wordplay: the Day comes 'like destruction (shod) from Shaddai'; God makes the heavens tremble and the earth shake from its place on the day of his wrath; God makes mortals rarer than fine gold, humans than the gold of Ophir; God stirs up the Medes, who care nothing for silver or gold; God musters his consecrated ones and mighty men; a host from the end of heaven, the weapons of his wrath; Ruined city never reinhabited, even by Arab tents or shepherds; inhabited by desert creatures, ostriches, jackals and dancing goat-demons (se'irim); Stars and constellations (kesilim) give no light, the sun is dark at its rising and the moon does not shine; The people's terror is like the pangs of a woman in labor with her first child; Oracle headed 'massa' (burden) against a named nation or place; The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness; Brief oracles against neighboring nations (Amalek, Kenite, Asshur, Kittim).

Only in The quake of the Hour and the proofs from embryo and rain: Some are returned to the most abject age so that after knowing they know nothing; In catastrophe mothers abandon their young and pregnancy fails [divergence between the texts]; Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped; In the catastrophe the father disowns his wife and the mother her child ('This is not my child'); In the catastrophe mothers, cows or she-camels no longer care for their young; God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews; On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls; Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

leads.title: Song of the vineyard; six woes; the nation from afar ↔ Rejected prophets, ruined towns, the thousand-year day and Satan's insertion
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Scoffers ask the prophet to hasten the punishment; it is held back only by an appointed term and will come suddenly (weight 6.6). Pair score 6.6.

Only in Song of the vineyard; six woes; the nation from afar: Woe to those who rise early for strong drink and feast with lyre and harp but ignore God's work; God raises a banner and whistles for a nation from the ends of the earth to come as his instrument; Woe to those who join house to house and field to field until there is no room left; Parable-song of the beloved's vineyard that yielded wild grapes despite all care and is abandoned to briars; The invading army never tires, sleeps or loosens belt or sandal; its horses' hooves like flint, its roar like a lion; Prophetic paronomasia: hoped for mishpat (justice) but got mishpah (bloodshed), for tsedaqah but got tse'aqah (outcry); God speaks to the snow 'Fall on the earth' and commands the downpour; Hypocrite men and women enjoin wrong and forbid right and close their hands; Refrain: 'For all this his anger is not turned back and his hand is stretched out still'; Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, darkness light and bitter sweet; God sends the flood of al-'Arim (the dam) and turns the two gardens into bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote-trees; Scoffers ask 'Lord, hasten to us our share (qittana) before the Day of Reckoning'; and 8 more.

Only in Rejected prophets, ruined towns, the thousand-year day and Satan's insertion: Destroyed towns lie fallen on their roofs, with an abandoned well and a lofty palace; It is not the eyes that are blind but the hearts within the breasts; Satan casts something into every prophet's recitation or wish; God abrogates it and confirms his verses; Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them [contrast between the texts]; Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them [divergence between the texts]; YHWH will be king over all the earth; in that day YHWH will be one and his name one; A thousand years in God's sight are like yesterday when it passes, or a watch in the night; The listeners walk among the dwellings of generations God destroyed, a sign; A foolish people who have eyes but do not see and ears but do not hear; The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

leads.title: Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo ↔ The quake of the Hour and the proofs from embryo and rain
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped (weight 7.3); God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.2.

Only in Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo: Darkness is not dark to God; night shines like day, darkness and light are alike; 'YHWH, you have searched me and known me': God knows sitting and rising, thoughts from afar, every word before it is spoken; 'Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? I hate them with perfect hatred'; 'If I take the wings of the dawn (shahar) and dwell at the far end of the sea, even there your hand leads me'; No soul dies except by God's leave at a term written (kitaban mu'ajjalan); Speaker was made in secret and embroidered (ruqqamti) in the depths of the earth; No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but it is in a Book before God brings it into being; Nothing wet or dry but is in a clear book; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record; Nowhere to flee God's spirit: if I ascend to heaven you are there, if I make my bed in Sheol you are there; and 14 more.

Only in The quake of the Hour and the proofs from embryo and rain: Some are returned to the most abject age so that after knowing they know nothing; In catastrophe mothers abandon their young and pregnancy fails [divergence between the texts]; The quake of the Hour: every nursing mother forgets her suckling, every pregnant one miscarries, people seem drunk though not drunk; In the catastrophe the father disowns his wife and the mother her child ('This is not my child'); In the catastrophe mothers, cows or she-camels no longer care for their young; On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls; Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

leads.title: Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo ↔ Migrants provided for; the night and day, the held sky, a rite for every nation
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God's eyes saw the speaker's unformed substance (golem); all his days were written in God's book before one of them existed (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo: Darkness is not dark to God; night shines like day, darkness and light are alike; 'YHWH, you have searched me and known me': God knows sitting and rising, thoughts from afar, every word before it is spoken; 'Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? I hate them with perfect hatred'; 'If I take the wings of the dawn (shahar) and dwell at the far end of the sea, even there your hand leads me'; No soul dies except by God's leave at a term written (kitaban mu'ajjalan); Speaker was made in secret and embroidered (ruqqamti) in the depths of the earth; No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but it is in a Book before God brings it into being; Nothing wet or dry but is in a clear book; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; God's knowledge of a person's thoughts and words, from afar or from near [divergence between the texts]; God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead bodies, and with him is a preserving record; Nowhere to flee God's spirit: if I ascend to heaven you are there, if I make my bed in Sheol you are there; and 15 more.

Only in Migrants provided for; the night and day, the held sky, a rite for every nation: God holds back the sky from falling onto the earth except by his leave; Those who emigrated for God and were killed or died will receive a fine provision; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); He holds up the sky (so that it does not fall on the earth); The sky falls, or is kept from falling, on the earth [divergence between the texts]; They sacrificed to shedim (demons), no-gods, new gods their fathers did not know; The god (alone) holds the heavens (and earth) in place: the bond or rope of heaven, holding back the sky; God makes the night pass into the day and the day into the night; Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth (lex talionis); I kill and I make alive, I wound and I heal; there is no god beside me; God visits the earth with rain, softens it with showers, and crowns the year with harvest; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted.

leads.title: Psalm 148, praise from heaven and earth ↔ Six communities judged; all things prostrate; garments of fire and bracelets of gold
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The place of humans in the worship offered by all creation [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); All in heaven and earth prostrate to God: sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, beasts and many humans (weight 7.3). Pair score 15.1.

Only in Psalm 148, praise from heaven and earth: Kings and peoples, princes and judges, young men and maidens, old and young together praise God; God commanded and they were created; he established them forever with a decree (hoq) that will not pass; Sun, moon and shining stars are summoned to praise God; Sea monsters (tanninim) and all deeps are summoned to praise God from the earth; 'The waters above the heavens' are summoned to praise; Fire and hail, snow and smoke, stormy wind fulfilling his word; God's angels, mighty ones who do his word, and all his hosts and ministers are summoned to bless him; Those near God do not disdain to worship him; they glorify him and prostrate; Heaven, earth, seas and all that moves in them praise God; The 'statutes of the heavens' (huqqot shamayim) and their rule over the earth; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David [divergence between the texts]; The seven heavens, the earth and everything in them glorify God, though humans do not understand their praise; and 5 more.

Only in Six communities judged; all things prostrate; garments of fire and bracelets of gold: Hooked maces of iron (maqāmiʿ) drive back those who try to escape hell; God will judge between believers, Jews, Sabians, Christians, Magians and polytheists on resurrection day; In hell the unbelievers are cut garments of fire and boiling water is poured on their heads, melting their insides and skins; Catalogue of bridal finery: embroidered cloth, tahash sandals, linen, silk, bracelets, necklace, nose-ring, earrings and a crown; In paradise the righteous are adorned with gold bracelets and pearls and wear silk; The host of heaven bows down to God; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

leads.title: Psalm 50 - God summons heaven and earth; do I eat the flesh of bulls ↔ Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving (todah) and pay your vows to Elyon (weight 7.7); God does not need sacrifices: 'If I were hungry I would not tell you... Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?' (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.6.

Only in Psalm 50 - God summons heaven and earth; do I eat the flesh of bulls: Superscription ascribes the psalm to Asaph; Every beast of the forest is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills, and the ziz of the field; God's faithful ones made a covenant with him by sacrifice; Our God comes and is not silent; fire devours before him and a tempest rages around him; Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines forth (hofia); 'I kept silent, and you thought I was one like yourself'; An oath invoking God by a repeated triple title (El, Elohim, YHWH); Whether God is in need and humans rich [contrast between the texts]; God rebukes the wicked who recites his statutes and covenant yet consorts with thieves and adulterers; Poet summons heaven and earth to listen; Wonder done 'so that you may know that the earth belongs to YHWH'; God summons heaven and earth to the judgment of his people in a covenant lawsuit; and 3 more.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); What is done with the blood of sacrifices, and whether it reaches God [divergence between the texts]; Whether the deity eats (receives) the food and drink of the offerings [divergence between the texts]; and 14 more.

leads.title: Psalm 56, when the Philistines seized David in Gath ↔ Migrants provided for; the night and day, the held sky, a rite for every nation

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).
